factions.name: The Order of the Long Watch
factions.description: A scattered chapter of vigil-keepers dedicated to the virtue gods. They keep faith through the night, tend the shrines, and can read which god's signs are present in a place. Reliable, slow, and in danger of losing a chapter.
factions.agenda: Complete the vigil-rite before the chapter's authority lapses. Find the novice. Reconsecrate the iron shrine to the right name before the garrison's faith sets around the wrong one.

factions.name: The Crimson Brotherhood
factions.description: Former soldiers and devoted fighters who have let KHORRUN's gaze become their purpose. They believe violence is prayer. They are effective, terrifying, and heading toward something they call a final reckoning.
factions.agenda: Consecrate the iron shrine. Bring the garrison's mood to a point. The Red Hour's devotees believe they are preparing for a war; they are preparing for an offering.

factions.name: The Hollow Merchant's Guild
factions.description: A trading consortium whose founding merchant was claimed by HAGRETH three generations ago. Most members do not know this. The signs are everywhere in their books if you know what to read. The wealth is real. The loyalty of it is not.
factions.agenda: Maintain the flow of trade. Find who has been drawing on the old accounts. Settle the debt that the founding merchant's heir does not know exists.

threads.name: The Red Hour's Mark
threads.description: KHORRUN's gaze has been on the garrison since a surrendered man was killed there three months ago. The mood is wrong, the shrine road is busy, and the Crimson Brotherhood is arriving in ones and twos. Nobody has connected the pattern yet. The garrison commander either has not noticed or has chosen not to.

threads.name: The Coinmother's Debt
threads.description: HAGRETH claimed the guild's founder three generations ago. The debt has been compounding since. The founding patron entry in the ledger is the hook; the heir who reads it has not reported what she found; the coins are arriving more frequently now, which means the reckoning is approaching. What HAGRETH calls in her debts nobody has described and survived to document.

threads.name: The Mirror-Crowned
threads.description: Lord Verran has been feeding VAUNTRETH for years without knowing the name of what he was feeding. He is not a villain — he is a man whose self-importance has been reinforced at every turn until it is indistinguishable from his identity. The lord who wants the shrine rededicated is not acting from greed or malice; he genuinely believes his name belongs above the original inscription. VAUNTRETH has been slowly reducing his ability to hear the word no.

threads.name: The Grey Tide
threads.description: ACEDIEL found Novice Davin in the vigil tower. The grey quiet that stopped him two hours before dawn is not a personal failure; it is a visitation. The chapter does not know this. If the novice's vigil-break is treated as cowardice rather than a sign, something real will be missed — and the vigil-rite will be rendered void for reasons nobody understands. ACEDIEL does not act with force. It simply makes the next step feel impossible.

threads.name: The Green Eye
threads.description: ISS turned its gaze on Cembra Vael when he burned his rival's workshop. The rival's best work was inside and is now gone from the world. Cembra has not completed a piece since. He thinks the block is his. ISS will continue consuming every thing Cembra tries to make until either Cembra understands what he did, or ISS grows bored and moves to someone with a more interesting rival to destroy.

threads.name: The Unbroken Furrow
threads.description: Somewhere in the grey roads, a labor was begun by a dead person and left unfinished. The laborer still working it does not know what it is for. ERRAN's presence is on it: tools that don't break, a second wind at exhaustion's edge, work that holds. The question is not whether the labor should be completed. The question is what completing it opens.

threads.name: The Surveyor's Route
threads.description: Aldous Vane approaches newcomers in the first village with warm enthusiasm, genuine historical knowledge, and a tour pamphlet. He is the single most dangerous person in the settlement and also the most useful: every site he recommends is real, historically significant, and lethal. He always waits at the entrance. He takes notes. He has been quietly feeding KHORRUN's consecration calendar for nine years through guided tours of places made holy by prior violence, treating each death as a form of historical annotation. The notebook is the investigation key — early pages are pure history, recent pages describe deaths in the same tone. The Brotherhood's consecration route maps are his pamphlets. The arc runs from charming local color to revealed Brotherhood logistics arm entirely at the player's pace: the player may take three tours and never look sideways, or look sideways on the first one. The augur knows; the prior does not.

threads.name: The Convergence
threads.description: The augur at the hill has named four gods active in the same region at the same time and said nothing about why. This has not happened in her thirty years on the hill. She reads signs; she does not issue warnings. The four convergent gazes — KHORRUN, HAGRETH, VAUNTRETH, and ACEDIEL — suggest something approaching, not something already here. Whatever it is, the Order of the Long Watch is not large enough to meet it alone.
